issue: Invented appliance placement and storage extent
detail: New copy: "A griddle and a pizza oven anchor the two ends of this twelve-foot Emory island, leaving counter space between them for prep and plating" and "storage underneath the full length of the counter". The source description is the generic Range boilerplate: it says only "spacious countertops, generous storage" and never states where the appliances sit or how far the storage runs. The title gives only "12-Foot Outdoor Kitchen Island with Built-In Griddle & Pizza Oven". Appliances at the two ends with counter in between is a fabricated layout that the product photo could directly contradict. Fix: say the island carries a built-in griddle and a pizza oven with counter space and storage, without asserting positions.

issue: Invented counter layout around the griddle
detail: New copy: "A single built-in griddle sits in this nine-foot Emory island, with counter space to either side for prep and serving." The source says only "spacious countertops" and never places the griddle centrally or claims counter on both sides of it; the title is just "9-Foot Outdoor Kitchen Island with Built-In Griddle". Drop "to either side".

issue: Invented counter layout around the grill
detail: New copy opens "One built-in grill, nine feet of galvanized steel island, and counter space on both sides of the cooking area." Same fabrication as the 9-foot griddle listing: the source boilerplate says "spacious countertops" only and states nothing about the grill's position or counter on both sides of it. The follow-on sentence ("would rather have counter room than a second appliance taking up the run") is built on that invented premise.

issue: Invented door mechanism (openable top half)
detail: New copy: "its working half door lets kids swing the top open and lean out or shut themselves in." The source says only "a working half door" — nothing about a separately opening top section or Dutch-door action. Sibling slug caraway-cottage-light-brown handles the same feature correctly ("A working half door opens into the cottage"). Reduce to what the source states.

issue: Invented slide dimension "8-foot wave slide" in both description and excerpt
detail: The source for this SKU never gives a slide length. Its description reads "then can ride the twisty tube slide or speedy wave slide back to the ground" and the title is "Atlas Steel Swing Set with Tube Slide"; the strings "8-foot", "8 foot", "8ft" and "eight-foot" appear nowhere in that product's title, description or highlights (highlights is empty). The new description says "A twisting tube slide and an 8-foot wave slide give two different rides off the same deck" and the excerpt repeats "a twisting tube slide and an 8-foot wave slide off one clubhouse deck". The sibling SKUs atlas-swing-set, atlas-swing-set-with-monkey-bars and atlas-steel-swing-set-with-tube-slide-and-monkey-bars DO state 8-foot in their sources, so the figure appears to have been carried across from a sibling. Fix: drop the length and say "wave slide" (the writer's own facts_kept list also wrongly records "8-foot speedy wave slide" as a kept fact).

issue: Frame described as "galvanized tube"; source never specifies tube stock
detail: New description opens "Just under 10 feet tall and entirely steel: galvanized tube under a powder-coated finish". The source only ever says "powder-coated steel", "premium galvanized steel" and "Angled A-frame made from heavy-duty powder-coated galvanized steel" — the substrings "tube", "tubular" and "square" do not occur anywhere in this product's title, description or highlights. Square-tube steel is a spec belonging to the Atlas products, not this one. Fix: "galvanized steel under a powder-coated finish".

issue: Adds an unsourced mechanism for the brasero firebox
detail: New text: "while the brasero firebox feeds coals to the cooking area for the smoky character that defines the style". The source only says "the brasero firebox infuses your food with rich, smoky flavors that define Argentine grilling" — it makes no claim about the firebox feeding or transferring coals to the cooking area, and the word "feed" does not appear in the source. Lower severity than the two above since it is a functional description rather than a spec, but it is still a claim the source does not support. Fix: keep the smoke/flavor claim and drop the coal-feeding mechanism.

issue: "Cedar gables and detailing" — source attributes gables and detailing to steel, not cedar
detail: Source: "Substantial cedar posts and beams combine with steel roofing, gables, and detailing that balances natural warmth with architectural precision." The list reads steel roofing / steel gables / steel detailing; the only cedar named anywhere in the source is the posts and beams ("oversized cedar timber"). The new line "Cedar gables and detailing warm up what is otherwise an engineered frame" reassigns the material of two components. Title ("Lodge | 14x12 Cedar and Steel Gazebo with Steel Roof") does not resolve it either. Fix: say cedar posts and beams under a steel roof with steel gables and detailing, or drop the gables clause.

issue: "rated for high winds and heavy snow" upgrades a performance sentence into a published rating
detail: Source says only "The steel roof is engineered for demanding climates, performing reliably through high winds, heavy snow, and year-round exposure." No wind or snow rating is stated. The new excerpt says the roof is "rated for high winds and heavy snow" and the description repeats "rated to hold up under high winds, heavy snow." In a Merchant Center feed "rated" reads as a certified figure. The three sibling gazebos correctly used "engineered"/"performs through", so this one is the outlier.

issue: "covers a patio table and seating" is a capacity claim absent from the source
detail: Final sentence: "The 14x12 size covers a patio table and seating without taking over a small yard." The source description says nothing about furniture, seating capacity or what fits underneath; the only dimensional fact available is 14x12 from the title. Delete or reduce to the bare footprint.

issue: "cedar gables and detailing" — same material flip as the other Lodge gazebos
detail: New text: "The frame is oversized cedar timber, with cedar gables and detailing that keep the natural warmth of the wood in view." Source groups gables and detailing with steel ("combine with steel roofing, gables, and detailing") and names cedar only for posts, beams and timber. Same fix as 14x12.

issue: "suits a centered seating arrangement or a dining table with room to walk around it" — unsupported capacity claim
detail: Opening sentence asserts what the 14x14 span accommodates. The source is the shared Lodge boilerplate and contains no furniture, layout or capacity information; 14x14 comes from the title alone. This is the writer inventing differentiation between four products whose source copy is byte-identical.

issue: "cedar gables and detailing" — same material flip as the other Lodge gazebos
detail: New text: "oversized cedar timber posts and beams carry the load, with cedar gables and detailing giving the frame its warmth." Source assigns gables and detailing to steel. Only posts, beams and timber are cedar in the source.

issue: "enough covered floor for a full outdoor dining setup or a seating group with circulation space" — unsupported capacity claim
detail: Nothing in the shared Lodge source describes covered floor area, furniture fit or circulation space. The only dimensional fact is 16x14 from the title. Same category of invention as the 14x12 and 14x14 furniture sentences.

issue: "Cedar gables and detailing" — same material flip as the other Lodge gazebos
detail: New text: "Cedar gables and detailing carry across the longer elevation." Source: "cedar posts and beams combine with steel roofing, gables, and detailing." Gables and detailing are steel in the source, cedar in the rewrite.

issue: "runs long enough to hold two zones" / "a dining end and a seating end" — unsupported capacity claim, and it is in the excerpt too
detail: The excerpt ("runs long enough to hold two zones under one powder-coated steel roof") and the opening sentence ("long enough to hold two things at once under one roof, a dining end and a seating end, without either crowding the other") both assert a usable-capacity fact. The shared Lodge source contains no layout, zoning or furniture information at all; 19x14 comes from the title. Because it is in the excerpt it becomes the meta description, so this one is the highest-exposure instance.

issue: "freestanding" is an installation claim the source never makes
detail: New excerpt: "An 8-foot by 6-foot freestanding privacy screen..." and new description: "Eight feet wide and six feet tall, this freestanding panel blocks sightlines..." The word appears nowhere in the source. Source title is "Privacy Wall 8x6" and the source description says only "Standing 6 feet tall and spanning 8 feet wide", "robust aluminum posts ensure lasting stability through any weather", and "ready-to-assemble design". Nothing states the panel stands unanchored rather than being mounted or staked, so "freestanding" asserts a structural/installation property that was invented. Verified: grep for freestanding/free-standing over the source title, description and highlights returns nothing. Dimensions themselves (8 ft x 6 ft), cedar + aluminum, airflow, hot tub/dining use, the Add-On Kit and ready-to-assemble are all correctly sourced.

issue: Invented operating mechanism for the brasero firebox
detail: New description: "the brasero firebox burns wood down to coals that get raked under the grates for smoke and flavor." The source only says "the brasero firebox infuses your food with rich, smoky flavors that define Argentine grilling." It never says the firebox reduces wood to coals, that coals are moved under the grates, or that anything is raked; grep for rake/raked/coals over the source returns nothing (the only adjacent fact is "the included coal shovel simplifies maintenance"). The claim is plausible for a real brasero grill but it is a design/operation detail added by the writer, not carried from the source. Everything else in this item checks out: wood and charcoal, multi-height heavy-duty steel grates, S-hooks for sausages and ribs, refractory fire bricks, ceramic fire blanket, 12-gauge powder-coated steel, acacia side table and handles, lower rack, coal shovel, BILT app.

issue: Excerpt asserts a wind and snow rating the source never claims
detail: New excerpt: "a gable roof rated for wind and snow." The source says only "The steel roof is engineered for demanding climates, performing reliably through high winds, heavy snow, and year-round exposure" — engineered for, not rated for. Wind and snow ratings are specific published figures (mph wind load, psf snow load), and this catalog carries real numeric ratings on other outdoor products, so "rated for" reads as a certification the source does not support. The 14x14 and 18x14 copy handles the same source line correctly with "engineered for demanding climates." Fix by matching them: "a gable roof engineered for demanding climates."

issue: "rated for" indoor/outdoor use where the source says "designed for"
detail: New description: "and it is rated for both indoor and outdoor use." The source reads "Designed for both indoor and outdoor use, it comes with heavy-duty casters." Nothing in the source or title claims an indoor/outdoor use rating, and "outdoor-rated" is a real product-certification term used elsewhere in this catalog (outdoor-rated refrigeration), so the swap upgrades a design-intent statement into a compliance claim. One-word fix: "designed for both indoor and outdoor use."

issue: Claims the smaller Honeywell packs come with a heavy-duty brass can tap; two of them do not
detail: The description ends: "This listing covers the cans themselves; the smaller Honeywell packs on the site are the ones that arrive with a heavy-duty brass can tap in the box." There are five smaller Honeywell 8oz listings in the catalog and only three of them include a tap. Titles: 'Honeywell R-1234yf Refrigerant - 8 Cans (8oz Each), Genuine - Made in USA' and 'Honeywell R-1234yf Refrigerant - 8oz Self-Sealing Can, MVAC Use - Made in USA' name no tap, and neither source description mentions one. The writer's own copy for the 8-can listing confirms the contradiction: it calls that pack 'a restock quantity for a shop that already owns a can tap.' A buyer reading the 16-can page is told the smaller packs ship with a tap, orders the 8-can or single-can listing on that basis, and receives cans with no way to connect them. The same sentence also asserts by implication that the 16-can case has no tap, which neither its title nor its source description states either way.

issue: igvagas boilerplate still ships in the highlights field on all 20 products (not in the new description/excerpt)
detail: The rewritten description and excerpt are clean, but the highlights array on every one of the 20 records in this batch is untouched and still reads: "At igvagas, we provide premium R-1234YF/R-134A/R-22 ... Refrigerant solutions for HVAC, automotive, and commercial refrigeration systems. Our products are:" followed by the checkmark bullets. src/app/products/[slug]/page.tsx lines 247-256 renders highlights.slice(0, 4) under a visible 'Highlights' heading, so the competitor name plus the 'premium ... solutions' filler is published on each product page directly beneath the new copy. Flagged here because it defeats the point of the rewrite even though highlights were outside the writer's per-product output; the field needs to be cleared or regenerated from the same fact list before these go live.

issue: Excerpt calls the Sarasota "freestanding" — a mounting characteristic the source never states
detail: New excerpt: "A freestanding 10x10 steel louvered pergola with drainage and gutter guards in the posts...". The source description for 10x10-sarasota-louvered-pergola never says freestanding or self-supporting; it only mentions "powder-coated steel posts and anchoring plates" and "downspouts in the steel posts" — and the wall-mounted Evanston in the same batch also has posts with downspouts, so posts do not establish it. Freestanding vs wall-mounted is a material purchase decision, and the writer appears to have inferred it by contrast with the Evanston rather than from the source. Drop the word or replace it with something the source supports.

issue: Product-line size claim "the smallest of the four Stratford sizes" is not in the source description or title
detail: New description opens: "The 12x10 Stratford is the smallest of the four Stratford sizes...". The source description (byte-identical across all 8 Stratford SKUs) never mentions how many Stratford sizes exist or which is smallest; its only size-adjacent phrase is the competitor comparison "part profiles 3X larger than standard small-footprint kits". The title supplies only "12x10". The claim does happen to match the current assortment (12x10, 14x10, 14x12, 16x12), so it is not false today, but it is sourced from the catalog lineup rather than from the product copy and silently becomes wrong the moment Range or the store adds or drops a Stratford size.

issue: Product-line size claim "The largest of the four Stratford sizes" is not in the source description or title
detail: New excerpt opens: "The largest of the four Stratford sizes, this 16x12 black pergola...". Same defect as the 12x10 black entry and doubly exposed because it sits in the excerpt, which becomes the meta description and Open Graph description. The source text carries no size-lineup information at all and the title carries only "16x12". Fix by dropping the superlative and the size count (e.g. lead on part profiles, which the description already does well in its body).

issue: Size claims "compact" and "keeps to a small footprint" have no basis in the source
detail: Excerpt begins "A compact cedar playhouse..." and the description's first sentence ends "...the Sweetwater Playhouse keeps to a small footprint." The original source description contains no dimension, footprint, square-footage or size-suitability language whatsoever — a search of it for size, sizes, small, compact, footprint, square, feet and dimension returns nothing. This is a fabricated dimensional claim in a Merchant Center-bound field. Note the contrast with the sibling sweetwater-heights-elevated-playhouse, whose "footprint modest for smaller yards" is at least anchored to the source phrase "perfectly sized for any outdoor space"; Sweetwater Playhouse has no such anchor. Remove both words.

issue: "carved corbels" is not in the source
detail: New description opens: "Dual structural cross beams, heavy support posts, and carved corbels carry the trellis roof...". The source (verified against git HEAD:data/catalog.json, since the working copy was overwritten mid-audit) says only "Thoughtfully crafted with dual structural cross beams, robust support posts, and elegant corbels". Nothing in the description, title, or highlights says the corbels are carved, and no highlights exist for this SKU. "Carved" asserts a construction/finishing detail about a physical component that the manufacturer copy does not claim. The sibling 24x12 Beaumont, working from word-for-word identical source text, correctly writes just "corbels" - so this is an addition, not a reading of the source. Fix: change to "corbels" or "elegant corbels".

issue: Cross-product material claim not in the source and contradicted by the catalog
detail: New text: "The wood is Nordic spruce rather than the cedar Backyard Discovery uses on its larger sets." The source description for Fall River says only "Built from robust Nordic spruce and finished in a light brown stain" - it says nothing about cedar or about what other Backyard Discovery sets are made of. The claim is also false against data/catalog.json: dover-bay-swing-set-with-tube-slide ($1,999, 242kg) and dover-bay-swing-set-with-monkey-bars ($1,699) are both described as "premium Nordic spruce", and spruce-hollow-swing-set ($1,499, 241kg) as "durable spruce" - all substantially larger and pricier than Fall River ($799, 60kg). Backyard Discovery demonstrably does use spruce on larger sets. Fix: end the sentence at "The wood is Nordic spruce, finished in a light brown stain."

issue: Pricing claim written into product copy
detail: New description closes with "The left-hand version is a separate listing at the same price, and the two cover either way a corner can turn." The price parity is true today (both emory-corner-outdoor-kitchen-island-and-bar-left and -right are 649900), but nothing about price appears in the source copy, and a price statement embedded in a Merchant Center description goes silently stale the moment either listing moves. The sibling rewrites make the same left/right point without it (e.g. the -left version says "Range builds the mirrored right-hand version as a separate item"). Fix: drop "at the same price" and keep "The left-hand version is a separate listing."

issue: New copy adds a serving "counter" that the source never mentions
detail: New text: "A snack bar window along one wall opens onto a counter, which is where most of the pretend cafe and tea party business ends up happening." The source description mentions only "The snack bar window adds another layer of fun, perfect for hosting delightful tea parties or running a cafe" -- it names a window, never a counter, and never says which wall it is on. Same fabricated element reappears in timberlake-playhouse ("a snack bar window opens onto a counter"), whose source likewise says only "A built-in snack bar window creates opportunities for creative play." Low-stakes as fabrications go (a counter is arguably entailed by "snack bar"), but it is a physical component present in neither source, and the fix is a one-word trim in both products.

issue: Excerpt claims the slide is "molded", a manufacturing/material claim absent from the source
detail: New excerpt: "...molded in a single piece with high side walls..." The entire source description is three sentences and says "One-piece construction makes installation a breeze and is designed to hold 250lbs." It never states that the slide is molded, nor what it is made of. Every other fact in this entry checks out (10-foot and yellow from the title, high side walls, one-piece, 250 lb, Backyard Discovery). Suggest reverting to "one-piece construction". Note: the 327-char description is below the 450 floor but that is permitted here -- the source is only ~340 chars and the writer used all of it.

issue: Excerpt opens with an unsupported and false size-ranking claim: "The larger Beaumont"
detail: The excerpt begins "The larger Beaumont in 100 percent cedar...". The Beaumont source description is identical across every size and never ranks or compares sizes, so nothing in the source or title supports a comparative. It is also false against the catalog: the Beaumont line has eight sizes (10x10, 12x10, 12x12, 14x10, 14x12, 16x12, 20x12, 24x12) and 16x12 (192 sq ft) is only third largest, behind 20x12 (240 sq ft) and 24x12 (288 sq ft). This is the meta description and OG description, so the wrong claim ships to search results. Note the writer's own facts_kept for this product lists no size-range verification, unlike the Windham, Ridgeline, Evanston and Sarasota entries which explicitly cite catalog checks. Fix by dropping the comparative and leading with the cedar/trellis fact.

issue: Claims the PowerPort works "without a cord running back to the house" — no power or wiring claim exists in the source
detail: New text: "A PowerPort set into the gazebo supplies three electrical outlets plus USB ports, which covers lighting and music without a cord running back to the house." The entire source sentence on this feature is: "Easily charge your devices, add cozy lighting, and enjoy your favorite tunes using our exclusive PowerPort, featuring three electrical outlets and USB ports to create the perfect ambiance." The source says nothing about how the PowerPort is supplied, and a mains outlet block in a gazebo does require a feed from a supply, so the clause asserts an installation characteristic that is both unsourced and likely wrong. The outlet and USB counts themselves are correct — only the trailing clause needs to be cut.

issue: "naturally durable against rot and decay" — the Norwood source only says "natural durability"
detail: New text: "built from 100 percent cedar and naturally durable against rot and decay". The Norwood source's only cedar sentence is "Expertly crafted from high-quality 100% cedar, this wooden gazebo delivers elegant style and natural durability." The words rot and decay appear nowhere in this product's description or title (verified against the original catalog). The phrase has been carried over from the Arcadia and Barrington copy, which do say cedar is "naturally resistant to rot and decay". The writer's own facts_kept line for this product reads "natural durability (source)", which does not support what was written. Fix by writing "naturally durable" and stopping there.

issue: "naturally durable against rot and decay" — the Norwood source only says "natural durability"
detail: New text: "The frame beneath is 100 percent cedar, naturally durable against rot and decay, trimmed with black steel accents." The 16x12 Norwood source carries the same single cedar sentence as the 14x12: "Expertly crafted from high-quality 100% cedar, this wooden gazebo delivers elegant style and natural durability." Neither "rot" nor "decay" occurs in this product's source description or title. Same imported-from-a-sibling-product problem as the 14x12 Norwood; trim to "naturally durable".

issue: "naturally durable against rot and decay" — the source only says "natural durability"
detail: New text: "Structurally it is 100 percent cedar, naturally durable against rot and decay, under a 29-gauge galvanized steel roof...". The Peak Roof Gazebo source says only "Expertly crafted from high-quality 100% cedar, this wooden gazebo delivers elegant style and natural durability."
